title: Opening and the importance of composing
summary: Rowe introduces Jackson and asks about composing; Jackson says Art Blakey stressed writing to find your individuality.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m very pleased to have saxophonist and composer Javon Jackson with me today, for the Jazz Archive.
Thank you. I’m looking forward to your concert here. But I wanted to start off asking you a little bit about something that I’m guessing is important to you and that is your composing.

I’m getting more involved with composing, very much involved with it now as the years have gone on. Joining Art Blakey, that was something that he really emphasized for us to do, writing, and it is very important to find your own self and some sense of your individuality through your own writing, so that’s very important.
